title: Engineering Understanding of Fault Detection in a CAT 994K Loader: A Comparative Study of Individual Data Streams
content: This paper presents a single-modality diagnostic study of three independent data streams collected over two years from a Caterpillar 994K wheel loader operating in a copper mine in Chile: high-frequency Vital Information Management System (VIMS) telemetry, oil analysis, and maintenance records. Each stream is analysed independently through modality-specific preprocessing and feature engineering. VIMS provides 1 Hz measurements, supplemented by condition-triggered trend summaries at largely hourly intervals; oil sampling is scheduled by operating time, at nominal intervals of 250 hours for the engine and 500 hours for the transmission. Maintenance records provide retrospective context for recurrent engine, torque converter and transmission interventions. The telemetry analysis shows a strong association between fuel rate and engine load, while operating hours explain less than 4% of fuel-rate variation. Load-normalised fuel performance remains broadly stable across approximately 14,000 operating hours. Unsupervised screening identifies elevated temperature observations, particularly around 140-150 °C for the torque converter outlet and 100-110 °C for transmission oil. Agreement across multiple anomaly detectors identifies a robust subset of observations for targeted engineering investigation. Oil analysis shows a pronounced transmission copper excursion around April 2024. Comparison with stable additive and lubricant-degradation indicators supports interpretation of the excursion as localised mechanical activity rather than generalised lubricant breakdown. The results also indicate compartment-specific monitoring roles, with transmission oil supporting event-focused investigation and engine oil providing a comparatively stable long-term condition baseline. A traceable TEDS index prioritises four fault candidates according to temporal detectability, economic impact, data richness, and statistical strength, while parts-level patterns help reconstruct related maintenance pathways. Looking at them individually, these findings show that useful diagnostic interpretation depends on separating operational demand, lubricant service history, and maintenance decision processes. The contribution of this paper is an application-based characterisation of the information and limitations of each stream, together with physics-informed procedures for prioritising diagnostic investigation.
